sense.text:
An ambassador is an accredited diplomat sent by a country as its official representative to a foreign country. That is what the brothers are: ambassadors, sent ones.

God asks, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And Isaiah answers, “Then said I, Here am I”. The prophet volunteered: Lord, send me. That is the same spirit as each and every one in the room. This is for the brothers, because they are the ambassadors, the bold witnesses for the kingdom.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” God does nothing before he reveals it through his prophets. So when the Bishop, the deacons and the captains tell our people to prepare, prepare, prepare, it is because we read the scriptures and see it in the scriptures.

The news shows where America is going. The president told hundreds of generals and admirals that there is a war from within and an invasion from within, and that the dangerous cities should be used as training grounds for the military. In their mind it is them versus us, and the target is the black man. The National Guard has been sent into 19 states so far, and next year is America’s 250th year. Something is going to happen. Watch and pray; watch the news; pay attention to your surroundings; and don’t put nothing past this white man.

One way or the other America is going to have a civil war. It is not if, it is when. In a civil war there is a curfew and you cannot leave your house, and even if you have the money the stores will not be open. There are different kinds of famine: one where there is no food; one where the food is there and you cannot afford it; and one where you have the money and the food may be there, but you cannot reach it. Prepare your mind. Prepare.

Black people have nothing to lose. They already took everything: our name, our culture, our identity. We have been dealing with it for over 400 years. We are used to it. And the reason to be glad is that our salvation is near.
“And they that consent unto them shall be had in derision and in reproach, and trodden under foot.” We read this scripture all the time to put it in our people’s minds.

“For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” This is not going to be in one city. It may not touch every city, but it will be in different cities. A great insurrection is talking about civil war.

“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” So don’t think there is not going to be a time when they come after us. They are going to come.

Some think what is seen in other countries could never happen in America, because America makes people believe it is the greatest and the most powerful. That is mistaken; that is not what the Bible said. The Bible tells what is going to happen here; the problem is not believing it. We are the doctors and our people are the patients: we give the medicine, the scriptures, and it is up to them to take it. We lead the brothers the right way, and we cannot use a weapon to force anyone.

“The burden of Egypt.” The Egypt here is America. “Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.”

“And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother”. That is what is seen in America right now: they are turning against each other, as with Charlie Brown that just got killed. The Most High is showing that they are turning on one another.

They worry about us, but our weapon is the Bible. We don’t have any weapon to fight against them. With this little book the Most High God is going to take America down, by us teaching it. Our weapons are not carnal; our weapon is spiritual. We are in a spiritual fight. No knife, no gun: all you need is your Bible. Study this book and be an expert in it; that is what you were called to do.

Go out there and wake up our people; that is the war. Our job is to save our people with the word of God, to change our people’s minds, and that is the greatest warfare. Our people are in desperate need and looking for a solution, and we are the solution.

“The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms”. Jeremiah, Isaiah, Nehemiah, Nahum, Micah, Malachi: all those prophets did the same thing we are doing today. There is no difference. We are those prophets. Whatever you were doing when you were here before, you came back to do it again: prophesy and teach, that our people may repent and come back to the Most High God’s laws. We are God’s witnesses, the proof that there is a God in Israel.

America is a great kingdom; France is a great kingdom. Look at what is going on in France right now: it is judgment time. Remember what they did to the Israelites in IUIC over there. We prayed for judgment and the Most High God showed us judgment. We pray the Most High God bring the whole government down for the evil done to our people in Haiti, Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali, and destroy every single one of them. No feeling sorry for them.

“The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the Lord hath truly sent him.” Some think the word of the prophet will never come to pass, but we show in the scriptures what is coming to pass right in front of our eyes, and some leaders are still playing games, still playing video games.

When you come to a certain age in this truth, not physical age, there are things you cannot do any more: a way you cannot dress, a way you have to carry yourself, a way you have to talk. Some are still in a kid mentality, wrinkled shirt and wrinkled pants. You are an ambassador. An ambassador is a representative to a foreign country, and the kingdom of God is foreign to our people: we represent the kingdom of the Most High and we represent Christ. An ambassador is also a promoter, and we promote the law, telling our people to come back to the Most High. You are somebody important.

A leader has to be active; you cannot be a leader if you are not leading anything. Coming in and sitting for seven, eight years is not what the Most High God called you to do. As the Bishop says, you cannot force a brother to do what he does not want to do; his spirit has to be in it.

“And for me, that utterance may be given unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly, to make known the mystery of the gospel”. 15,000 churches could close in the US this year, and those who call themselves Christians have dropped from 78% to 62%. The article will not say the Israelites have anything to do with it, but God’s spirit is back in the earth. The teaching the brothers do in the street is affecting the whole world; the coast of Africa is rising up. Christ said the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. Even if something happened to us tomorrow, they cannot stop this. It is bigger than you and me, and the enemy will come after us because we are bringing our people out of darkness into the light.

“For which I am an ambassador in bonds: that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.” Paul was an ambassador in bonds, that he might speak boldly. That is the spirit every brother should have.

When you teach this Bible you have to look alive and put some life into it. Some teach like they don’t believe what they are saying, and if we can tell, the enemy can tell. Some were in gangs in the world, doing crazy stuff, and now in the truth they are all shy. This is not the time to be shy; this is the time to make your voice heard. Teach it like it is the last day, your last time on planet earth.

“For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ”. Our conversation is the way we talk to each other, and the way we talk to people in the world. Your conversation should be about this Bible, not sports.

On the job some of them know you are an Israelite, yet one out of every three words is a curse word. That is not godly conversation: it is about sport, or look at this big butt sister over there. You want that brother or sister at your job to repent, but your conversation does not match what you teach. As leaders and ambassadors, understand that they are always watching you. We look for the Saviour, so there are certain things you have to watch that you say.
“Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth”. James is speaking of the power of the tongue.

“And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity”: a world of sin. “So is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body”. The thing you say can defile the whole body, with your mouth. It “setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.”

Stand a hundred men here and pass one word around; by the time it reaches the hundredth man it has already changed. That is why the tongue sets on fire. Be careful what comes out of your mouth.
“For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind”. Man tames everything, even the lion in the jungle.

“But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil”. You have the power on your tongue to build and the power on your tongue to destroy. What are you going to use it for?

As a man of God, the same tongue you use to tell brothers and sisters to repent, you find in conversation you are not supposed to be in, and some don’t even catch themselves. Some are very disrespectful to each other. It cannot be so in here. We deal with that disrespect outside; in IUIC there is order, and everybody has to follow that order. We are raising up respectful men, and we must respect each other.

“But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” God says, Fear not. He has called us by his name, and we are his.

“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord”. We are God’s witnesses. “And my servant whom I have chosen”: God has chosen us, “that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.”

Not Jehovah’s Witnesses: God says it again and again, we are his witnesses. A witness is one who bears witness that something happened, who saw it with his own eyes and experienced it. The Lord gives us his prophecies; when we go out speaking them and they come to pass, we are witnesses that his word is true.
“I, even I, am the Lord; and beside me there is no saviour.” Beside God there is no saviour.
“I have declared, and have saved, and I have shewed, when there was no strange god among you: therefore ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, that I am God.”
“Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.” If God had sent us to another nation, they would have heard us. But God sent us to the Israelites.

“But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.” Our people are hard-headed, and the job is not going to be easy, but we chose to do the job. There was a time that was us; we were hard-headed too, and now, praise the Messiah, we are here today.

“Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads.” Our people have a hard face, especially Judah; when you go to talking to Judah, they look like they want to kill you. God has made your forehead harder than theirs. Don’t be afraid of that face; they aren’t going to do anything.

“As an adamant harder than flint”: adamant is something really, really hard, and it also means refusing to be persuaded or to change one’s mind. God gave Israel the power over this Bible. Whatever IUIC says the scripture says, that is what it says, and we do not care about the opinions of the apologetics and the other camps. We don’t care about your opinion, just like God don’t give a damn about your opinion. The scripture says one wife, one husband, and that is what we teach. You can go out and find a hundred scriptures and have as many hoes as you want; we don’t care. That is what the prophets in IUIC say, and God don’t care about anything else.

“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: the children of thy race. Read with verse 7, the children of thy people are the house of Israel. God did not send us to other nations; he sent us to the house of Israel. A little kid can see it, yet grown ass men who claim they went to school, to so-called seminary school, cannot understand this. This is for you dumb Christians.

Why “them of the captivity”? History shows we are the only people who went into slavery on slave cargo ships. We did not come here voluntarily. We are the captives, the children of the captivity.

“And speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” We, the leaders, the teachers, the prophets, the apostles, have no choice.

precepts.why:
Some think they have a choice, so Jeremiah 1. The words of Jeremiah came “in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign”, on to Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, “unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

Then the word of the Lord came: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”. Before I formed thee means before your mother was even pregnant, before you were in your mother’s womb, God knew you. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: before your mother gave birth, God sanctified you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

A leader’s, a prophet’s destiny is chosen for him. Your destiny was chosen for you; you cannot choose your own destiny. God ordained you a prophet. That is why, whether our people will hear or whether they will forbear, we have no choice but to go and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God.

sense.text: This is for the apologetics, Esau and all of them who have no authority over this Bible. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob”. Jacob’s name was changed to Israel, and Jacob had 12 sons. We are the descendants of those 12 sons: the so-called African Americans, the so-called blacks, the so-called Hispanics, the so-called Native American Indians make the 12 tribes. “His statutes and his judgments unto Israel”: not unto Esau, not the Chinese, not the white man. Unto Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”: not with the Chinese, not with Amalek, not with Moab. God only deals with us. The Bible is for the Israelites, by the Israelites. Nobody else has any authority over this book, and we do not care about their opinion.

“Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.” Men of understanding means men that have understanding of the scriptures, and known among you.

The IUIC is a government, God’s army. Esau understands his own government: a president, vice president, Congress, senators, a secretary of defense, governors, mayors, chiefs of police, councilmen, starting from the top. Some served in Esau’s military and understand that, yet cannot understand the Most High God’s government, though the Bible explains how it works. The mind has to change.

As Gil Noble said, an oppressed people have to organize and create their leaders, the way the poor people in Montgomery anointed Dr. King. The enemy does not want to see us organized. Moses was picked by the Most High God to lead the people out of Egypt, and the people rebelled and wandered forty years until they all died. In IUIC there are programs, men of valor and others, to build the men up: a brother becomes a soldier, then an officer of 10, 20, 50, then captain, deacon, bishop. Where there is no order, there is chaos.

We are the only people who step into a position and do not understand what the position expects. Some want to be an officer only to tell people what to do. Leadership is painful; your household is a reflection of you, your wife and your children. You won’t see the president in a strip club or a bar, and a leader cannot move the way a young man moves.
“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.”

“So I took the chief of your tribes”: the men seen on the screen are the chief of your tribes. “Wise men”, wise in the scriptures, not in the things of the world, “and known, and made them heads over you”: officers, captains, deacons, bishops, “captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds”.

These men have to understand the role they step into. It is not easy leading men, because we are dealing with a rebellious people. What is expected of an officer of 50 is not what is expected of an officer of 10. The higher you rise, the higher the expectation.

Leadership is difficult from within and from without: jealousy and rivalry within, abject hatred without. All the camps and Esau hate IUIC, but a dog does not chase a parked car; it chases one that is moving. IUIC is strict and does not bend the law for anybody, though some of our people have itching ears. We will keep doing the work, going places no man has been before.
“The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.”

“Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”. The high mountain is America, France, those high powers; the banner is the Bible. He is telling us to teach this Bible. “Exalt the voice unto them”: the them is the Israelites, our people. “Shake the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.”

There are consequences that come with what we are doing; that is why they go into the gates of the nobles. They spent billions of dollars doing what we are undoing, and they are not just going to let us wake our people up. If you don’t want to get burned, get the hell out of the kitchen; don’t play with fire. We are not going to sugarcoat it. This is not going to be a walk in the park; set your mind like that.

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” All of us must conform to the image of Christ.

That change starts in the mind. Our minds have to be conformed; they call it being born again, formed, constructed. We are all sick in the mind, and that is where the war starts. You cannot teach something you are not living up to.

“Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.” The old man must die: the weed head, the crack head, the coke head, the adulterer. That old man has to go. You have to be reformed.
He that is dead is free from sin: he that destroyed the old man is free from sin. You cannot carry the old man and the new man; one of them has to die.
“Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him”.
“Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.”
“But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for it were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void.”
“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!”

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward”. If I teach the gospel willingly, not forced, I have a reward. Nobody forces the brothers to do anything; you have to have the spirit to do this willingly. “But if against my will”, if somebody forced me to do it, “a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” A dispensation is a time period.

“What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.”

In the church of Corinth they did not want to help Paul. Paul travelled to many places, by boat, in the sea for weeks at a time, visiting some churches over and over, and somebody had to pay for those trips. The brothers at Corinth would not help him.
“For though I be free from all men, yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more.” At the end of the day we are servants. Our job is to serve the people.

“And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law”. Paul made himself weak to win the brothers over. He is not saying he went and committed sin. He is not saying, they invited me to Thanksgiving dinner, so I went to win them over. His job was to gain brothers and sisters over to this gospel, “being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ”.

The video of the Bishops sending out the call to the pillars, to awaken the people and stir the bones of the sleeping, to undo what Esau spent billions to weave, was played to strengthen the brothers’ spirit. Then: “I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom”.

“Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.” Our job is to reprove and rebuke, and to exhort. Exhorting each other is one of the things black people cannot do.

“For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears”. There are a lot of Israelite camps out there after their own lusts.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” We are that preacher. Our people are thirsty for this word and waiting on the brothers to bring them this clean cup of water. Do not let our people down.

“And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is us.

The good news is: I’m an Israelite, and Jesus is a black man. Here in the States it is taken for granted, but many on the planet have never heard it, nor know it is in the Bible. The brothers spent a month in Sierra Leone teaching it every single day for 30 days, and many had never heard it before. It is a beautiful thing to wake up and realize Christ looks like me. The people depend on the brothers; they are the only ones who will bring the good news.

“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel”. We are the watchmen. The watchman watches for danger, and our job is to warn our people what is coming so they can prepare themselves.

We are watchmen over the house of Israel. Our responsibility is only to our people; our people come first. The Chinese love their own people and nobody calls them racist; Donald Trump makes it clear he only cares about his people and nobody calls him racist. When the Israelite says he only cares about his people, everybody says, you’re racist. Well, hell, be it then: I’m racist then, because the truth is I don’t give a damn about nobody else but my people. That does not mean not helping a child about to be hit by a car; it means my people come first. Everybody else cares about their own nation; y’all dumb Christians, something is wrong with y’all.

“Therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.” The word of God’s mouth is this Bible. When we open the Bible we give our brothers and sisters warning of what is coming: repent, for the kingdom of God is at hand; keep the law.

“When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life”. Our job is to go to the wicked and tell the wicked to repent and leave his wicked ways, to save his life.

This is how it sounds to people in the street. “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” A lot of people think we are a bunch of fools, saying all we do is stand in the street yelling at people. But it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching.

There was no mic when Christ spoke to 5,000 people, and the Bible describes his voice as the sound of many waters. He was not whispering, repent, the kingdom of God is at hand. He was talking real loud. Your Christians are stupid as hell; they don’t even read this Bible at all.

precepts.why:
“Cry aloud, spare not”: talk loud and spare none. We are not supposed to care about anyone’s feelings. “Lift up thy voice like a trumpet”: a trumpet is loud. So when we teach we are supposed to raise our voice, because we are not only talking to the person in front of us; we are talking to everybody.

People put up videos saying all we do is scream at people. We are not screaming at anybody; we are teaching the Bible, as the scripture says to, loud like a trumpet. That is the foolishness of preaching.

sense.text: “For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh”: not many wise men in the world, “not many mighty, not many noble, are called”.

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise”. We are the foolish things. Nobody is like us: everything wrong in America is blamed on the black man. When Charlie Brown got killed, the blame went to the black man, and they went to the black college threatening us, though it had nothing to do with us. Even when Esau kills each other, it is the black man’s fault. That is how we know we are the sons of God, the gods the Bible says we are.

“And God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”. We are the weak things of the world, and they are not going to see us coming, because we do not come with knives or guns; we come with the word of God. They look at us as a bunch of men in the street yelling and screaming, yet the government of France shut us down, and no other Israelite camp. They take us very seriously.

Unity and order bring fear to the heart of the white man: a thousand black men in one place with no fight, no gunshot, no smoking; hundreds of sisters sitting quietly, reading the Bible, paying them no mind. That brings fear.
“Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.” We are ambassadors.
“For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.” The him he made to be sin is Christ. Christ knew no sin.

“Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few”. Some look at us and say there are a lot of them; the Bible says that is not enough. Israel is like the sand of the sea, and Christ said we are not going to reach all Israel.

“Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” God is the Lord of the harvest. When you pray, pray for more labourers: that the Most High God send more brothers and put this spirit on more brothers to teach this word. Our people are dying out there and nobody cares about them except us. We are the labourers; that is the job of the leaders, the prophets.

“For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.” The Most High God is not going to forget the brothers. As Paul said, there is a reward: for the work, the bricks, the blood and sweat put into this truth.

And the sisters: if you make a sandwich for a brother, for a prophet, you have ministered to the saints, and God is not going to forget that. There is a reward for that. Just as we need the men, we need the sisters too; we need each other to build this kingdom.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. This is a spiritual war; we are at war. “That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” We are soldiers, and our job is to please him who chose us, and not get entangled with the things of the world.

You have to work; the Most High God understands that. But the office in corporate America is not your office. If the owner puts a Christmas tree in it, go in there, do your damn job and go home; argue with the owner about it and you are going to lose your damn job. When people at work say let’s go to the bar after work, you have a wife and kids; what the hell are you doing in the bar? Then you commit adultery and say, oops. Do not put yourself in that position thinking you can control it. Make something up, but do not get entangled, or you end up breaking God’s laws.
“And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.” You have to strive lawfully.

precepts.why:
“And this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you. Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize?” A bunch of brothers are running, and only one receives the prize. “So run, that ye may obtain.” You obtain it by keeping the law. Don’t get entangled in anything; don’t let anything keep you from that crown or let anybody take it away. Everything here is going to get burned.

“And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things.” That is what Timothy said: striving for the mastery. The mastery of this world, the trophies of a sports team or a black belt in martial arts, are temporary. “Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.” The reward we want is the eternal reward.

“I therefore so run, not as uncertainly”. Paul ran in this truth certain, 100%, that he would get the reward, because he believed and had faith. “So fight I, not as one that beateth the air: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. Every sin has to be brought into subjection: lust, money, anything that keeps you from the goal, the kingdom of heaven. As Christ said, whatever keeps you, cut it off, whether your wife, your husband, your children or the job.

“Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” Don’t be a hypocrite; do what you tell others to do. You cannot tell brothers and sisters to repent and be in a bar drinking with them, with a ho all over the place, then make an excuse that you almost committed adultery; something is wrong with you. Paul is saying, be the perfect example. You cannot tell your cousins, your uncle, your mother and father to repent and then be smoking weed with them, eating turkey at Christmas dinner or at a birthday party. You’re a joke; they look at you as a joke, a hypocrite. Because of you the word of God is blasphemed, and there is a judgment for that.

sense.text: “But watch thou in all things”. You cannot watch if you do not watch the news. As leaders you have to know what is going on in the world and what time you are in, so you can warn your people. The sisters can have an excuse, because they are not called to be leaders; the brothers are, and have no excuse. Endure afflictions. “Do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry”: make full proof of your ministry by doing the work.
“For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.” Paul is telling us he is about to die.

“I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith”. Whatever you sent me to do, Lord, I did it; I kept the law. If your time came right now, could you say that? If you can’t, step up to the plate and do more.

“Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day”. Paul understood the work he was doing and knew a crown was waiting for him. “And not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.” Paul was talking about the brothers doing the same work he was doing.

Not everybody is going to be on the same level in the kingdom of God. No kingdom has everybody on the same level; there are going to be levels.

“All scripture is given by inspiration of God”: every single scripture is given by the Most High, “and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness”: to instruct our people in righteousness. Those are the things the prophets use to better the people: to reprove, to rebuke, to correct and to instruct them in righteousness.
“That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.” Are you the man of God? Then by these scriptures you may be perfect.
